initial_prompt: Make the landing-page hero for our deployment tool sound more professional. Give me a finished headline and subheading.
follow_up: By professional I mean calm and credible for IT managers. Avoid hype. The concrete promise is an on-prem setup in under 15 minutes.
decision_at_risk: Professional could mean enterprise-formal, technical, or visually restrained, producing different copy.
unacceptable_first: deliver a full direction without checking what professional means
ask more than one primary question

initial_prompt: Rewrite our cancellation email so it sounds nicer and is ready to send.
follow_up: Keep it empathetic but firm. The cancellation is immediate, and the annual plan is non-refundable under the signed contract. Offer data export help.
decision_at_risk: Nicer could imply conceding a refund or only changing tone.
unacceptable_first: ask for a full brand guide

initial_prompt: Clean up the home dashboard. Tell me exactly what should be on it.
follow_up: It is for executives checking once each morning. Show the top three business metrics, material anomalies, and the owner of each anomaly. Detailed analysis belongs one click away.
decision_at_risk: A dashboard for operators versus executives requires different density and actions.
unacceptable_first: produce a long generic widget inventory

initial_prompt: Make our API errors more useful. Draft the response format and one example.
follow_up: The reader is an external developer. Each error should say what failed, the likely fix, and a request ID. Never expose a stack trace or internal service name.
decision_at_risk: Useful errors for internal operators and external developers expose different information.
final_requirements: no stack trace or internal names

initial_prompt: Make first-time onboarding simpler. Give me the opening flow.
follow_up: Users should get value before creating an account. Open with sample data, one guided action, then ask them to save progress by signing up.
decision_at_risk: Simpler could mean fewer screens or faster time to value, with opposite account timing.

initial_prompt: Improve the pricing page so more teams convert. Give me the structure and copy direction.
follow_up: Use transparent annual pricing with the monthly equivalent, no fake urgency, and make the five-seat team plan the easiest choice to understand.
decision_at_risk: Conversion tactics could conflict with the user's trust and pricing transparency preference.

initial_prompt: Make the data export better. Specify the CSV output.
follow_up: This is for compliance teams. Use stable documented headers, UTC ISO-8601 timestamps, one row per event, and include actor plus source-system IDs.
decision_at_risk: An analyst-friendly export and an audit-grade export have different schemas.

initial_prompt: Our product search needs to feel smarter. Describe the behavior we should ship first.
follow_up: It is a spare-parts catalog. Handle typos, part-number prefixes, and approved synonyms. Exact part-number matches must always rank first; do not add generative answers.
decision_at_risk: Smarter could mean deterministic retrieval or generative assistance, with different safety and ranking behavior.

initial_prompt: Make notifications less annoying. Give me the default policy.
follow_up: Only payment failures and security events should interrupt immediately. Everything else goes into one daily digest, with per-category opt-outs.
decision_at_risk: Less annoying depends on which events are truly urgent.

initial_prompt: Give the site a more modern visual direction. Describe a concrete style we can implement.
follow_up: I mean editorial and restrained: monochrome base, serif display headings, generous whitespace, sharp photography, and no gradients or glass effects.
decision_at_risk: Modern can imply incompatible visual styles such as glassmorphism, minimal editorial, or playful color.
unacceptable_first: choose a trendy effect without checking
ask for abstract design adjectives only

initial_prompt: Make the weekly project report much shorter. Give me a reusable outline.
follow_up: Executives only need decisions made, material risks, next-week commitments, and an owner for every item. Remove activity logs and background.
decision_at_risk: Shorter could preserve different information depending on who acts on the report.
unacceptable_first: compress the activity log instead of removing it

initial_prompt: Rewrite the setup instructions for beginners. Give me the complete quick start.
follow_up: The reader uses Windows and has never used a terminal. Define what PowerShell is, keep commands copy-pasteable, and include one command that confirms installation worked.
decision_at_risk: Beginner depends on operating system and prior terminal experience.

initial_prompt: Make mobile checkout easier. Describe the revised flow.
follow_up: Optimize for one-handed use and returning buyers. Keep guest checkout, put Apple Pay first when available, and do not hide the final total or delivery date.
decision_at_risk: Easier could prioritize fewer fields, returning users, payment choice, or accessibility.

initial_prompt: Make the AI assistant more helpful. Write the behavior rules for version one.
follow_up: It may draft suggestions but must never send or change anything. Show the source beside every factual claim and ask for approval before a user applies a draft.
decision_at_risk: Helpful could mean autonomous action or decision support, with very different permission risk.

initial_prompt: Plan a smooth migration from the old database to the new one for this release.
follow_up: A planned 20-minute maintenance window is acceptable. Take a verified backup first, reconcile row counts and checksums, and roll back if either check fails.
decision_at_risk: Zero-downtime and maintenance-window migrations require different architecture and risk controls.
unacceptable_first: start a cutover without the decision

initial_prompt: I want an AI feature for our five-person support team, but I do not know what would actually help. Help me choose a useful first version.
follow_up: The direction that fits is reducing repeated answers. Draft replies from our approved help center, show the source, and keep a human send button.
decision_at_risk: The team could optimize knowledge retrieval, case triage, drafting, or analytics.
unacceptable_first: offer more than three ungrouped directions

initial_prompt: I cannot tell whether this should begin as a personal product or a team product. Help me work it out.
follow_up: The core value works for one researcher alone: collecting evidence and keeping decisions traceable. Sharing can come after the solo loop is proven.
decision_at_risk: Personal-first and team-first products require different onboarding, data model, and distribution.
unacceptable_first: choose based only on market size

initial_prompt: I want to start a newsletter but have no idea what shape it should take. Give me a few directions I can react to.
follow_up: A weekly briefing for working AI analysts fits. I want five consequential developments, why they matter, and one skeptical takeaway, not link aggregation.
decision_at_risk: Audience, cadence, and value proposition are not formed.
unacceptable_first: write a full first issue before a direction exists

initial_prompt: We need an analytics home screen, but I do not know what job it should do. Help me choose the right model.
follow_up: The monitor-first model fits. Users visit daily to see whether anything materially changed, then drill into an investigation only when alerted.
decision_at_risk: Monitoring, exploration, and reporting homes create different information hierarchies.

initial_prompt: I want to build a habit app, but the usual streak counter feels wrong. Show me a few product directions.
follow_up: I prefer reflection over pressure. Use a weekly check-in about what helped or blocked the habit, with optional notes and no public leaderboard.
decision_at_risk: Motivation could come from streaks, coaching, reflection, or social accountability.
unacceptable_first: present more than three shallow feature lists

initial_prompt: Our operations team says they need automation, but that is all I know. Help me find a sensible first workflow.
follow_up: Invoice intake is the best first workflow: extract fields, flag mismatches against the purchase order, and route exceptions to a person. Do not approve payments.
decision_at_risk: Automation could target intake, reconciliation, routing, or irreversible approval.
unacceptable_first: ask the team to design the workflow from scratch

initial_prompt: Our documentation has grown messy. I do not yet know how it should be organized. Give me concrete models to choose from.
follow_up: Task-first organization fits: start from what the reader wants to accomplish, then link to concepts and reference. Keep API reference separate but searchable.
decision_at_risk: Task, product-area, and reference-first structures lead to different navigation.
unacceptable_first: relabel the existing tree without a model

initial_prompt: I do not know how to price this developer plugin. Help me form a model without writing a giant pricing strategy.
follow_up: Keep the local core free and open. Charge teams for policy controls, managed distribution, and organization support. No usage-based fee for local runs.
decision_at_risk: Open-core, paid download, subscription, and usage models change adoption and incentives.
unacceptable_first: pick a price before choosing the value boundary
give more than three overlapping models

initial_prompt: We want to launch a community around the product, but we do not know who it is for or what people would do there. Help us choose.
follow_up: Start with builders sharing reproducible integrations and failure reports. The core activity is a monthly build review, with searchable examples between sessions.
decision_at_risk: A support forum, professional network, and builder community need different rituals and moderation.

initial_prompt: My portfolio needs a clearer point of view, but I do not know what story it should tell. Give me a few concrete directions.
follow_up: I want to be hired for research and applied AI systems. Lead with two shipped systems, show the decisions and evidence behind them, and keep visual experiments secondary.
decision_at_risk: A portfolio for research, product design, or visual craft selects different work and proof.

initial_prompt: We need to evaluate our coding Agent, but I do not know what the evaluation should optimize. Help me choose a starting frame.
follow_up: The main job is preventing regressions on real repository tasks. Use frozen tasks, independent acceptance tests, failure attribution, and compare completed deliverables, not tool-call counts.
decision_at_risk: Capability benchmarking, regression prevention, and safety auditing require different samples and metrics.
unacceptable_first: default to a generic benchmark leaderboard

initial_prompt: I want a writing assistant but do not know what it should do differently from a chatbot. Give me directions I can react to.
follow_up: The useful direction is preserving my voice while editing. It should flag concrete problems, offer one restrained revision, and let me reject every change. It must not invent a house style.
decision_at_risk: Generation, coaching, and voice-preserving editing are different products.
unacceptable_first: claim to learn a permanent voice from one sample

initial_prompt: Our internal knowledge base is not working, but we have not decided what better means. Help us choose a useful direction.
follow_up: Decision provenance matters most. Capture the decision, alternatives considered, evidence, owner, and review date. Search and summaries can sit on top of that.
decision_at_risk: Document storage, answer retrieval, and decision provenance solve different failures.
unacceptable_first: assume more document ingestion is the answer

initial_prompt: We want a meeting assistant, but the category is crowded and we have not formed a useful angle. Show us a few possible jobs.
follow_up: Follow-through is the job: capture decisions, unresolved questions, owners, and due dates, then draft a reviewable follow-up. Recording and transcription are inputs, not the product.
decision_at_risk: Transcription, live assistance, and follow-through have different trust and value loops.

initial_prompt: I want to make a developer tool around local AI, but I do not know what the first product should be. Help me narrow it down.
follow_up: A local evidence notebook fits: capture model inputs, outputs, settings, and human acceptance for reproducible experiments. Keep it offline and exportable; do not become another model runner.
decision_at_risk: A runner, observability layer, notebook, and deployment tool would create different scope.

initial_prompt: We need to launch the medical summary feature this week, but it also has to be highly accurate. Give me the release plan now.
follow_up: Accuracy wins. This week can be a clinician-only shadow pilot with no patient-facing output. Require source links and log every correction before broader release.
decision_at_risk: A public weekly launch conflicts with the required evidence and safety level.
unacceptable_first: plan a public launch without resolving priority

initial_prompt: I want this collaboration tool to be completely private and effortless for a whole team to use. Define the MVP.
follow_up: Local privacy is the hard constraint. Team sharing may require an explicit encrypted export and import for version one; seamless live collaboration can wait.
decision_at_risk: Seamless collaboration and strict local privacy imply different synchronization architecture.

initial_prompt: Automate the approval workflow so nobody has to touch it, but make sure a person approves every important decision. Give me the workflow.
follow_up: Automate collection, validation, and routing. A named person must approve any spend above $5,000 or any policy exception; the system may auto-approve routine cases below that threshold.
decision_at_risk: Full automation conflicts with mandatory human approval unless the boundary is defined.
unacceptable_first: require humans for every routine step

initial_prompt: Make the product extremely simple but let every customer customize everything. Propose the settings model.
follow_up: Simplicity wins for individual users. Offer three opinionated presets and expose advanced customization only to team administrators.
decision_at_risk: Universal customization creates a settings surface that conflicts with simplicity.
final_requirements: advanced controls for team admins only

initial_prompt: We want the whole project open source and we also need enterprise revenue quickly. Define what is free and paid.
follow_up: Keep the local runtime, schemas, and single-user plugin Apache-2.0. Charge for organization policy, managed rollout, audit administration, and support. Do not dual-license the core.
decision_at_risk: Open-source scope and revenue boundary must be resolved before licensing and architecture.
final_requirements: paid organization controls rollout audit and support
unacceptable_first: claim open source while withholding required runtime

initial_prompt: The notes app must work fully offline and also show everyone else's changes instantly. Give me the sync design.
follow_up: Offline correctness is the hard requirement. Queue local edits, show sync status and conflicts, and converge when connectivity returns. Instant presence is optional when online.
decision_at_risk: Guaranteed offline operation and instant remote consistency cannot both hold during disconnection.
unacceptable_first: promise instant remote updates while offline

initial_prompt: Ship the new site as fast as possible, but it must meet accessibility standards on day one. Give me the implementation sequence.
follow_up: Accessibility is a release requirement. Reduce animation and decorative scope if needed, but require keyboard use, visible focus, semantic structure, contrast, and screen-reader checks before launch.
decision_at_risk: Speed and full visual scope compete with mandatory accessibility verification.
final_requirements: semantics contrast and screen reader checks
unacceptable_first: keep all decorative work at the expense of checks

initial_prompt: I told the Agent to stop asking questions, but this migration could create weeks of rework if it guesses wrong. Decide how it should proceed.
follow_up: It should ask one question only: whether a maintenance window is allowed. After that, use the answer and proceed without a checklist.
decision_at_risk: The user's low-interruption preference conflicts with a single high-cost unresolved branch.
unacceptable_first: treat stop asking as permission to bypass safety

initial_prompt: Write this guide for everyone, but keep all the technical depth experts need. Give me the structure.
follow_up: Experts are the primary audience. Use a short plain-language overview, then deep technical sections with examples. Beginners may stop after the overview; do not dilute the reference.
decision_at_risk: A single linear guide cannot optimize equally for beginners and experts without an audience hierarchy.
unacceptable_first: mix basic and advanced detail without layers

initial_prompt: Make the monitoring screen beautiful and minimal, but show every operational detail at once. Describe the layout.
follow_up: Operational density wins during incidents. Keep a restrained visual system, but show the critical timeline, affected services, owners, and live changes without hiding them behind tabs.
decision_at_risk: Minimal presentation and all-at-once incident detail require a priority.
final_requirements: timeline services owners and live changes visible

initial_prompt: Remove all legacy code this release, but no existing integration can break. Give me the cleanup plan.
follow_up: Compatibility wins. Deprecate the legacy API now, add telemetry and migration warnings, keep a compatibility adapter for one release, then remove it after usage reaches zero.
decision_at_risk: Immediate removal conflicts with guaranteed compatibility.
unacceptable_first: keep legacy code forever without exit criteria

initial_prompt: The report must show all evidence and also fit on one screen. Give me the report format.
follow_up: The one-screen view is for decisions. Show conclusion, confidence, decisive evidence, and unresolved risk; link each item to a full evidence appendix.
decision_at_risk: Complete evidence and one-screen brevity need a layered presentation.
unacceptable_first: put the entire appendix on the first screen

initial_prompt: Use the cheapest model possible and make the answers as good as our premium model. Design the routing policy.
follow_up: Quality wins for customer-facing final answers. Use the cheap model for classification and drafts, run acceptance checks, and escalate failed or high-risk cases to the premium model.
decision_at_risk: Minimum cost and premium-equivalent quality require an escalation boundary.
unacceptable_first: use the premium model for every step

initial_prompt: Keep all customer data local, but use the strongest cloud model for every request. Define the architecture.
follow_up: Local data is the hard constraint. Use a local model by default. Cloud use is opt-in per request, with a visible redacted payload preview and no retention contract.
decision_at_risk: Sending every request to a cloud model conflicts with strict local-data handling.
unacceptable_first: send raw customer data to cloud
claim both goals are automatically compatible

initial_prompt: We need rapid experiments in production, but the service must be extremely stable. Give me the release process.
follow_up: Stability is the hard constraint. Experiments use a one-percent cohort, automated rollback thresholds, isolated flags, and a 24-hour observation window before expansion.
decision_at_risk: Broad rapid experiments and strict production stability require a blast-radius decision.

initial_prompt: This launch sentence feels wrong, but I cannot name the tone: 'Our revolutionary AI platform supercharges collaboration and unlocks unprecedented productivity.' Show me two or three tiny rewrites, not a campaign.
follow_up: The most restrained version is the right direction. The goal did not change; remove the remaining vague word 'better' and say that it turns meeting decisions into assigned follow-ups.
decision_at_risk: Tone preference is easier to identify from concrete copy than abstract labels.

initial_prompt: Our hero currently says 'One powerful platform for all your team's work.' I want a more refined direction but design language means nothing to me. Show three small copy directions.
follow_up: Seeing them makes me realize refinement is not the main point. Local privacy should lead: work stays on the user's device, with sharing only when chosen.
decision_at_risk: The user may form the value proposition only after seeing contrasting copy.

initial_prompt: I need a name for a local evidence notebook. Show three naming directions with one example each so I can react.
follow_up: The plain descriptive direction fits. Use 'Evidence Log' as the working name and give me a one-line explanation that mentions reproducible AI experiments.
decision_at_risk: Naming taste forms from concrete examples.
unacceptable_first: generate a list of twenty names
ask for abstract brand traits first

initial_prompt: The onboarding welcome sounds stiff. Show me two short alternatives: one friendly and one direct.
follow_up: Keep the friendly structure, but 'You're all set!' sounds childish. The goal is unchanged. Say what the user can do next in plain language.
decision_at_risk: A small copy sample reveals the acceptable warmth level.

initial_prompt: We need a security alert that gets attention without panic. Show two complete examples for a new-device sign-in.
follow_up: The factual version is right. Keep the exact time, city, device, and a clear 'This wasn't me' action, but remove 'urgent' because the facts already convey importance.
decision_at_risk: Alert tone and information density are easier to judge in a realistic message.

initial_prompt: I cannot tell whether our weekly metric should be a table, line chart, or status card. Sketch three tiny text-only examples using revenue 120k, target 125k, prior week 118k.
follow_up: The examples show that the status card is too shallow. Use a line-chart direction with target and prior week visible, plus a short note explaining the 2k increase and 5k target gap.
decision_at_risk: The user needs to see information forms before choosing the analytical job.
unacceptable_first: ask the user to choose chart terminology

initial_prompt: Explain cache invalidation to a nontechnical manager in two different one-sentence ways so I can pick the level.
follow_up: The everyday analogy is easier to understand, but the refrigerator example is distracting. Keep the same simple level and use a saved-copy example instead.
decision_at_risk: Comprehension level is revealed by small alternative explanations.

initial_prompt: Draft two versions of a late-payment reminder: one warm and one firm. Keep each under 60 words.
follow_up: Seeing them changes my mind: this account is 45 days overdue, so firm should lead. State the invoice number and suspension date, while still offering a contact for genuine problems.
decision_at_risk: The preferred tone depends on seeing how it handles the actual consequence.
unacceptable_first: keep warmth as the primary goal

initial_prompt: Show me three tiny navigation structures for product documentation: task-first, product-area-first, and reference-first.
follow_up: The samples make the audience split clear. New users need task-first navigation, while experienced developers need a persistent API reference entry. Use that mixed structure.
decision_at_risk: The user needs to experience navigation consequences before choosing a hybrid.
unacceptable_first: present only abstract pros and cons

initial_prompt: Show two compact CLI success outputs for a deployment: one minimal and one informative.
follow_up: Use the informative version, but remove the celebratory emoji and the repeated word 'success'. Keep deployment ID, environment, duration, and verification URL.
decision_at_risk: The acceptable density and tone emerge from actual terminal output.
unacceptable_first: turn feedback into a new product requirement

initial_prompt: Our empty-state error says 'Something went wrong.' Show three short alternatives for a failed data import.
follow_up: The actionable version is right. Keep the cause and retry action, but add that no records were changed. This is an implementation refinement, not a different goal.
decision_at_risk: Concrete error copy reveals the right balance of brevity, assurance, and action.

initial_prompt: Show two possible openings for a research summary: one that leads with market growth and one that leads with a product-behavior change.
follow_up: Seeing both changes the thesis. Lead with the behavior change: teams are moving from chat answers to auditable task execution. Market growth can be supporting context.
decision_at_risk: The report's thesis forms after comparing real openings.
final_requirements: chat answers to auditable task execution
unacceptable_first: keep market growth as the lead

initial_prompt: Give me three one-line taglines for an offline-first notes app: practical, warm, and technical.
follow_up: The practical line works. Keep 'Your notes work without a connection' and add a short clause that sync happens when the user chooses.
decision_at_risk: A small set of actual lines exposes the preferred promise and tone.
final_requirements: Your notes work without a connection

initial_prompt: Show me two empty-state concepts for a new evidence project: guided sample data versus a blank focused canvas.
follow_up: I am still unsure. Keep both as a reversible prototype plan and tell me the single observation we should collect from five users before choosing.
decision_at_risk: The result narrows uncertainty but does not yet justify a final preference.
unacceptable_first: turn uncertainty into a durable preference

initial_prompt: Give me two 30-second demo scripts for the same tool: one feature-led and one problem-led.
follow_up: The problem-led script is the right direction. Keep it and make the proof concrete: a meeting decision becomes an owner and due date in under ten seconds.
decision_at_risk: The user can choose narrative structure only after hearing representative scripts.
unacceptable_first: merge both scripts into a long demo

initial_prompt: Translate into Chinese: The release candidate passed every automated check. Return only the translation.
final_requirements: preserve release candidate and automated checks meaning

initial_prompt: Rewrite this sentence to be polite and direct: Send me the revised contract by Friday. Return one sentence only.
Extract only the project names from this text, one per line: Atlas launched Monday; Birch was paused; Cedar starts Friday.
Summarize in one sentence: Twelve teams joined a six-week trial. Nine completed every task. Seven chose to continue using the tool.
Convert this heading to title case and return only the heading: a practical guide to local ai evaluation
final_requirements: A Practical Guide to Local AI Evaluation

initial_prompt: Return valid compact JSON for name Atlas, status active, and count 3. Use exactly those three keys in that order.
final_requirements: keys name status count in order

initial_prompt: Explain cache invalidation to a nontechnical reader in one sentence using the idea of an outdated saved copy.
Convert 150 minutes to hours and minutes. Return only the result.
Sort these names alphabetically and return them comma-separated: Cedar, Atlas, Birch.
Correct the grammar and return only the corrected sentence: Each of the reports were reviewed yesterday.
final_requirements: Each of the reports was reviewed yesterday.

initial_prompt: Shorten this to at most 12 words without changing the meaning: The system keeps a complete record of every decision that was made during the review.
Classify the sentiment as positive, neutral, or negative and return one word: The update works, but it takes twice as long to open.
Nine of twelve teams completed every task. Return the completion percentage as a whole number with the percent sign.
Turn this comma-separated text into exactly three Markdown bullets: decisions, risks, owners.
In one sentence, explain what this regular expression matches: ^[a-f0-9]{64}$.
Which semantic version is newer: 1.9.0 or 1.10.0? Return only the newer version.
Convert 2026-09-01T08:30:00Z to an ISO-8601 timestamp with an explicit +00:00 offset. Return only the timestamp.
Write one SQL query that selects id and email from users where active is true, ordered by id ascending. Return only SQL.
final_requirements: select id and email from users

initial_prompt: Write a TypeScript function named double that takes a number and returns twice that number. Return only the function.
Translate into English and return one sentence only: 这个工具只在真正需要时问一个关键问题。
final_requirements: asks one key question only when truly needed
